Regulations Governing Language Requirements in the Language
of Instruction
(dated 25 April 2017)
The Extended Executive Board of the University has resolved:
§1 Basic Principles
1Foreign-language applicants for a Bachelor's, Master’s, or Teaching Diploma degree program must
provide proof of competence in the language of instruction of the respective study program or teaching
subject before they matriculate at the University of Zurich.
2The language skills required for matriculation at the doctoral level are assessed during the admissions
process by the institute/department or the graduate school, and/or the dean’s office/office of student
affairs.
3Foreign-language applicants refer to persons whose first or primary language is different from the
language of instruction.
4In these regulations, first or primary language should be understood as the language that a person
proficiently uses to write, speak, and understand written and oral statements without any difficulty.
This corresponds to reference level C2 or higher in the Common European Framework of Reference for
Languages (CEFR). 1
5At the University of Zurich, the languages of instruction used in the study programs and teaching
subjects are German and/or English.
6Proof of language proficiency of level C1 or higher in the Common European Framework of Reference
for Languages (CEFR) must be submitted for the relevant language(s) of instruction. 1
7Certain study programs or teaching subjects require language skills in other and/or further languages;
proof of these language skills must be submitted to the faculties either during the academic admission
assessment or in the course of the studies. Details are listed in the relevant program regulations.
§2 Recognized Language Certificates
The list of recognized language certificates with at least reference level C1 is determined by the
Admissions Committee in consultation with the Language Center and published as an appendix to
these regulations.

§3 Exemption from Proof of Language Proficiency in the Language of Instruction
Prospective students with one of the educational backgrounds listed below are exempt from providing
proof of language proficiency in the language of instruction:
− Federal or Swiss maturity certificate, or federally or Swiss recognized maturity certificate
− Federal professional maturity certificate in combination with proof of passing supplementary
examinations
− Specialized maturity certificate recognized in all of Switzerland in combination with proof of passing
supplementary examinations
− Maturità ginnasiale commerciale del Canton Ticino
− Bachelor's degree from UZH
− Bachelor's degree or comparable degree in the language of instruction that is relevant for the studies
from a university or university of applied sciences located in a region where official language is the same
as the language of instruction (does not apply to distance learning or studies at campuses in countries
where the official language differs from the language of instruction)
− Attendance of the last three years of upper secondary school in the language of instruction relevant for
the studies in a school located in a region where official language is the same as the language of
instruction
§4 Final Provisions
1These regulations enter into force on 1 May 2017 for admissions to studies from Spring Semester 2018
onward.
2The final German language test in accordance with the Regulations Governing the German Language
Test for Non-German-Speaking Prospective Students at the University of Zurich dated 26 May 2009 will
take place in August 2017, with a repeat exam offered in February 2018.
4 The Regulations Governing the German Language Test for Non-German-Speaking Prospective
Students at the University of Zurich dated 26 May 2009 shall be repealed as of 28 February 2018.
On behalf of the Executive Board of the University of Zurich
The President: The Secretary General:
Michael O. Hengartner Rita Stöckli
